attempts.lead: Costed activities show a combined spending shortfall of Rs 51.96 crore against plans, and the gap is spread across blocks rather than being confined to one location.
attempts.detail: The broad spread appears in 27 of 28 asset categories; Banking Facilities shows no clear pattern. Rangeilunda has the largest recorded gap at Rs 9.11 crore, with Rs 2.73 crore spent against Rs 11.84 crore planned, while Kalimela spent Rs 1.76 crore of Rs 7.65 crore. Blocks should review ageing activities and reconcile whether these gaps reflect works yet to start, incomplete expenditure records or plans that are no longer active; the sample does not by itself establish the cause.

attempts.lead: Recorded expenditure across the 20-GP sample was Rs 51.96 crore below planned cost, and the gap is spread across all 16 blocks rather than being driven by one block. Rangeilunda and Kalimela warrant first review because they show the largest shortfalls.

The broad block-level spread appears in 27 of 28 category groupings; Banking Facilities is the only grouping where no clear pattern was found. At the next review, ask blocks to reconcile planned costs with work status and recorded payments, particularly in Rangeilunda and Kalimela; these figures show lower recorded spending than planned, but do not establish whether this reflects delays, cancelled works or incomplete records.
